# Welcome to notes

Write in **Markdown**: headings with `#`, lists with `-`, and tasks you can tick:

- [ ] a task
- [x] a finished task

| Thing | Where |
|-------|-------|
| Keys | Drawer |

Share a note with a link, *view only* or *can edit*.
board.state.loading: Looking for this board on the network…
board.state.missing: Not found yet. It may still be on its way from a relay, or the relays have forgotten it. Keep this open — it appears as soon as a device that has it comes online.
board.state.deleted: This board was deleted by one of its editors.
board.state.locked: Boards are encrypted. Open this one with the full link you were given.
board.unlock.noKey: That link has no key for this board.
board.duplicate.title: Duplicate board
board.duplicate.text: Makes a new board with a copy of everything in this one and new links. Use it to cut off people you shared the old links with.
board.remove.title: Remove from your boards?
board.remove.textEdit: The board stays online for everyone else. Unless you have its link saved somewhere, you lose access to it.
board.remove.textView: The board stays online for everyone else. You can add it again with its link.
board.delete.title: Delete for everyone?
board.delete.text: “{title}” and everything in it is wiped for every device and everyone it was shared with. This can’t be undone.
board.error.viewOnly: You can only view this board.
list.emptyEdit: Nothing here yet. Paste several lines at once to add them all.
list.clearDialog.title: Clear done items?
note.heading: Heading
note.conflict: This note was changed on another device while you were typing.
note.placeholder: Write in Markdown… # headings, **bold**, - [ ] tasks, | tables |
note.tooLong: Too long to save — split it into two notes
share.title: Share “{title}”
share.explainEdit: Anyone with this link can read and change the board and share it on.
share.explainView: Anyone with this link can read the board, but not change it.
share.hint: The key is in the part after #, which never leaves the browser. Links can’t be revoked — to lock people out, use Duplicate and delete the old board.
account.title: Account & settings
account.backupText: One file with your key, your boards and everything in them, encrypted with a passphrase. Keep it somewhere safe — it restores everything even if every relay forgot you.
account.deviceTextSignedIn: Signing out removes your key and cached boards from this browser. Sign in again any time.
account.deviceTextKey: Wiping removes this device’s key and cached boards. Without an account, an exported key or a backup, boards only you had links to are lost.
account.wipeDialog.title: Wipe this device?

account.wipeDialog.text.one: This deletes the only copy of this device’s key. {n} board will be gone from this device unless you have a backup, the key or the links.
account.wipeDialog.text.other: This deletes the only copy of this device’s key. {n} boards will be gone from this device unless you have a backup, the key or the links.

account.how.1: Loadout runs on nostr: signed events on relays anyone can run. Every board is its own key pair; whoever holds the edit link signs changes as the board, and relays reject anything else for that board.
account.how.2: Edit links carry the board’s secret key, view links only the read key. Every title, item and note is encrypted before it leaves your browser; guessing a board’s address gets you ciphertext. A link is a key: whoever has it can pass it on, and links can’t be taken back.
account.how.3: The keys sit in the # part of the link, which browsers never send to any server. Opening a link moves them into your wallet and out of the address bar.
account.how.4: Your list of boards, with their keys, is encrypted to your own key and published under it, so signed-in devices stay in sync.
account.how.5: An account is your key, encrypted with your password and published under an address only your username and password can produce. Nobody can find, spam or overwrite it, and a wrong password simply finds nothing. The key itself works in other nostr apps too.
account.how.6: Changes made offline are kept on this device and sent when a relay is reachable again.
account.how.7: Relays can drop old data. Each device keeps every event it has seen and sends its copy back whenever a relay reconnects; relays keep the newest version of each item, so nothing old overwrites anything new.
account.how.8: Backups hold your key and every signed event, so a backup restores everything — even your account — when no relay and no other device has it any more.
account.backupDialog.title: Download backup
account.backupDialog.text: Choose a passphrase for the file. Without it the backup can’t be opened — by anyone, including you.
account.restoreDialog.title: Restore backup
account.restoreDialog.text: Restoring switches this device to the key in the backup. Boards already on this device are added to it, and everything the relays have lost is put back.
account.restoreDialog.noKey: The backup doesn’t contain a usable key.
backup.error.notBackup: This is not a Loadout backup file.
backup.error.wrongPassphrase: Wrong passphrase, or the file is damaged.
session.offlineLater: Offline — restored items will sync later
